verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Recovery: the Lean states the increment form ℛ(u+w, p+π) - ℛ(u,p) = … rather than the sum form, and splits the base velocity as u = B + a (background plus correction) with w = b, π = q. Unfolding linearResidual ε … B b q = ∂_t b + transport(B,b) + transport(b,B) + ∇q - ε Δb and adding the three explicit transports transport(a,b) + transport(b,a) + transport(b,b) gives ∂_t w + ∇π - εΔw + transport(B+a, w) + transport(w, B+a) + transport(w,w), i.e. ∂_t w - Δw + ∇π + (u·∇)w + (w·∇)u + (w·∇)w at ε = 1, using bilinearity of transport in each slot (transport_add_left at CorrectionStep.lean:237, transport_add_right at :245). Two encoding differences, both carried by the Lean as generalizations: the Lean keeps a viscosity parameter ε in front of the Laplacian where the paper's ℛ of (3.1) fixes viscosity one, and it works in the cylindrical moving frame (Vr, Vθ, Vz, Vt) with complex-valued components, so (u·∇)v is the frame transport with its angular generator and 1/R factor rather than the Cartesian directional derivative.
